title: Levantine/Sinai/Cypriot copper ores: monazite & radiogenic-heat geochemistry
question: Do Levantine, Sinai, or Cypriot copper ores — the material basis of the "singende Schlüssel" artifact — contain enough Th-232/U-238-bearing minerals (monazite/thorite) to produce a real (if nanowatts-scale) radiogenic warmth signature, and is the claimed phosphate-belt link to the Qatna/Amara region geologically defensible?
why_now: OTA-SCI-0080-2026-DE explicitly flags this as an open data gap: "[T — Datenlücke] Kupfererze aus Sinai/Zypern sind nicht systematisch auf Th/Monazit untersucht." The artifact's perceived warmth is a canonical physical claim in the Yin Hua Saga (NOXIA), the doc is a kueper.com publication candidate, and the metallurgy feeds SSF chemistry modules. Resolving it with geochemical literature (Sinai/Serabit el-Khadim, Cyprus/Troodos, Timna, Syrian phosphate belt) would either close the gap or let the curator harden the [T]/[S] classification honestly — directly serving the archive's R/S/F integrity principle.
